_meta.description: Tripura district & sessions court formatting rules — drives cause-title, party designations, prayer language, verification format
_meta.change_protocol: CLO sign-off required for any change. Vishal raises Jira tickets to Ajay for additions; never edits unilaterally.

designation: IN THE COURT OF DISTRICT & SESSIONS JUDGE
jurisdictionNote: District-level criminal and civil courts in Tripura, supervised by the High Court of Tripura (principal seat at Agartala). Tripura has 8 districts following the 2012 reorganisation. Bengali and English are the working languages under the Tripura Official Language Act, 1964; Kokborok (Tripuri) is recognised. The Tripura Tribal Areas Autonomous District Council (TTAADC) operates Sixth Schedule customary courts for tribal customary matters.

party_designation.state: State of Tripura through the Principal Secretary, Home Department, Government of Tripura, Agartala

case_nomenclature.atrocity_case: Spl. Sessions (SC/ST Atrocities) Case No. _____ of {year}

prayer_language.opening: It is, therefore, most respectfully prayed that this Hon'ble Court may graciously be pleased to:
prayer_language.closing: And for this act of kindness, the petitioner shall, as in duty bound, ever pray.

verification_format:
I, {deponent_name}, {designation}, do hereby solemnly verify and declare that the contents of paragraphs ___ to ___ of the above petition are true to my personal knowledge and the contents of paragraphs ___ to ___ are based on information received and legal advice tendered, which I believe to be true. Nothing material has been concealed therefrom.

Verified at {place} on this {date}.

DEPONENT
localRules: Bengali and English are working languages of the Tripura subordinate courts; pleadings before the High Court of Tripura are in English.
Bail applications under S.483 BNSS (formerly S.439 CrPC) must disclose prior rejections and be accompanied by certified copy of the FIR.
Anticipatory bail applications (S.482 BNSS) require certified copy of FIR and grounds; the High Court of Tripura is the preferred forum for serious offences.
Vakalatnama in the form prescribed under the High Court of Tripura Rules with requisite court-fee stamp.
Court-fee under the Court-Fees Act, 1870 as adopted by Tripura with State amendments.
SC/ST (Prevention of Atrocities) Act, POCSO and NDPS cases tried by designated Special Courts at the district headquarters.

TTAADC Sixth Schedule customary courts (Village Court, Subordinate District Council Court, District Council Court) under the Tripura Tribal Areas Autonomous District Council (Administration of Justice) Rules, 1991 retain jurisdiction over tribal customary matters; advocate must verify forum jurisdiction before filing in TTAADC areas (parts of Dhalai, Gomati, Khowai, North, South, Sepahijala, Unakoti, West Tripura).
e_filing_note: e-Filing operational at Agartala via eCourts portal; not yet mandatory state-wide.
